oewn-07501369-n.learner: a particular feeling of wanting something
examples: It was a passing want, and by morning she had forgotten it.

oewn-14472871-n.learner: the condition of needing something that is missing or that you cannot get
examples: The whole plan failed for want of money.
For want of a lamp, they sat in the dark.

oewn-09390888-n.learner: a thing you must have but do not have
examples: His wants were few: bread, a bed, and a fire.
When I am in company with him, I will not be wishing.
The favour of your company has been much felt, I assure you.

oewn-08201779-n.learner: a group of guests or friends gathered together socially
examples: She had the mortification of seeing Mary, after very little entreaty, preparing to oblige the company.

oewn-08074934-n.learner: a body set up to do business
examples: He left school and took a job at a shipping company.

oewn-01826886-v.learner: to feel concern about someone or something, or to be interested in them
examples: I should not care how proud I was.
I should not care about it myself; but the grounds are delightful.

oewn-02555993-v.learner: to look after someone and give them what they need
examples: She cared for her mother through the long illness.

oewn-01828678-v.learner: to hope for something, to want it, or to prefer to have or do it
examples: Would you care to walk with me before dinner?
Mrs. Jenkinson expressed her fears of Miss De Bourgh's being too hot or too cold.
She had no fear of its spreading farther, through his means.

oewn-07534492-n.learner: the strong feeling you get when you expect a particular pain or danger, which usually makes you want to run away or fight
examples: Fear held him still on the path as the dog charged.

oewn-07536278-n.learner: a feeling of very deep respect for someone or something
examples: He was raised in the fear of God.

oewn-01999581-v.learner: to move ahead, going onward through space or through time
examples: She was proceeding directly to her favourite walk.
They proceeded in silence along the gravel walk that led to the copse.
He paused, then proceeded: "As I was saying, the road was closed."

oewn-02377696-v.learner: to follow a set way of doing something, or to take a certain course of action
examples: She then proceeded to inquire into the measures which her father had intended to pursue.

oewn-02493222-v.learner: to go and see someone for a short time
examples: He had always intended to visit him, though to the last always assuring his wife that he should not go.

oewn-01847631-v.learner: to travel to certain places, for example to see the sights
examples: They visited Rome and Venice in the same summer.

oewn-02498679-v.learner: to go and see a place, for example for enjoyment
examples: On our last day in the city we visited the old castle.

oewn-00902866-v.learner: to make someone come to know another person face to face
examples: Are you much acquainted with Mr. Darcy?
Allow me to acquaint you with my sister.
He wrote at once to acquaint her father with the news.

oewn-00875857-v.learner: to make someone familiar with something, or well used to it
examples: You should acquaint yourself with the rules before you play.

oewn-04594951-n.learner: a frame of wood or metal holding a sheet of glass, built into a wall or a roof to let in light or air
examples: Miss Lucas perceived him from an upper window as he walked towards the house.
Its windows, opening to the ground, admitted a most refreshing view of the high woody hills behind the house.

oewn-04595668-n.learner: a clear opening in a vehicle that lets you see out at the side or the back, and that can usually be opened
examples: She rolled down the car window and waved to us.

oewn-04597048-n.learner: the sheet of glass set in a window
examples: A stone cracked the window, though the frame was not damaged.

oewn-06705943-n.learner: words that say you approve of someone and think well of what they have done
examples: "I deserve neither such praise nor such censure," cried Elizabeth.
This was praise of all others most extraordinary, most opposite to her ideas.

oewn-06706247-n.learner: the offering of words of honour as an act of worship
examples: The congregation lifted their voices in praise.

oewn-07081631-n.learner: the way a person speaks to another person
examples: He had all the best parts of beauty, a fine countenance, a good figure, and very pleasing address.

oewn-07253354-n.learner: the giving of a formal spoken message to a group of listeners
examples: He had risen to the honour of knighthood by an address to the king during his mayoralty.

oewn-08508037-n.learner: the place where a person or a group can be found or reached
examples: Their office address is on the second floor of the old mill.
